solver_notes: Native two-thread C11/pthreads lifecycle regression executed on RAK Miner v2 aarch64. Legacy PyEval_SaveThread model borrows a tstate without head_mutex or an owning reference; concurrent delete unmaps its page, and the daemon atomic decrement produces a REAL SIGSEGV (shell exit 139, pytest -SIGSEGV). Fixed SaveThread holds head_mutex across interpreter-list lookup and atomic refcount increment; Delete holds head_mutex for detach and drops the list reference atomically (2->1), the daemon drops 1->0, and exactly one final unmap/free occurs. Eight fixed regression iterations plus the main test pass. Scope is a standalone native model, not a claimed CPython upstream patch; the supplied repo torvalds/linux is inconsistent with Python/pylifecycle.c and is disclosed. Honest attempts retained: attempt 1 lacked _GNU_SOURCE for pthread barriers; attempt 2 hit a broken ASan allocator CHECK on this aarch64 runtime, so the final test uses mmap/munmap to produce a real memory fault without sanitizer dependence. file_sha256_of_this_json is SHA-256 of compact JSON with that field null; external payload SHA covers final bytes.

tests_run.command: gcc -std=c11 -O2 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pthread interpreter_lifecycle.c -o interpreter_lifecycle && ./interpreter_lifecycle legacy; test $? -eq 139 && ./interpreter_lifecycle fixed && python3 -m pytest -q test_frontier_0043.py
